title: The Page Object pattern and reusable components

videos.script: Three tests add fruit to the basket, and all three pass. {{three}} Then a developer renames one button. Add to basket becomes Add to cart. The shop still works. And all three tests fail, each after waiting thirty seconds for a button that is gone. {{red}} The tests were right about the shop. They were wrong about where they kept their knowledge of it. Every test held its own copy of every locator. {{copies}} This lesson moves that knowledge into one place, a page object. The tests say what a customer does. The page object knows where things are on the page. {{page-object}} The same rename now costs one line. {{one-line}} Then the page is cut into parts. A product card, the basket in the header. Each part becomes a small object of its own. {{components}} You will see why a page object should hand back a locator and not a number. A number is read once, and it races the page. {{race}} Then a fixture hands every test its page object, ready to use. {{fixture}} And the lesson ends with the opposite mistake. Wrapping everything, until nobody can see what a test does. {{end}}
